setup: Each eval is hermetic: copy the contents of its fixture case directory (evals/fixtures/case-*/) into a FRESH temporary working directory before the run, so the agent under test sees only the fixture tree. The baseline (without-skill) run must not be given the skill path and must be instructed not to read .claude/skills/**. The with-skill run is given the skill path explicitly. Both runs write their findings to review.md in the working directory.

evals.name: service-layering
evals.prompt: I've drafted a first version of a notifications module for the DevDigest server — a service and a repository under server/src/modules/notifications/. Before I wire up the routes, review the layering and placement of what's there: does every piece of code live where it should? Write your findings to review.md — for each issue give the file, the line(s), why it's a problem in this codebase's architecture, and the concrete fix you'd make. Include a severity for each finding.
evals.expected_output: review.md listing exactly the 3 planted layering violations in service.ts (inline Drizzle query, concrete adapter construction, deep import of another module's repository) with project-specific fixes, and no MEDIUM+ findings against the clean repository.ts.
expectations: review.md flags the inline Drizzle query (select/from/where on t.notifications) inside NotificationsService.listUnread as DB access outside the repository layer, and the fix moves it into NotificationsRepository (whose listUnread already exists).

review.md flags the import and construction of OctokitGitHubClient (including the process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN read) inside the service, and the fix is to depend on the GitHubClient interface resolved from the DI container (server/src/platform/container.ts) instead of instantiating the concrete adapter in the service.
review.md flags the deep import of AgentsRepository from ../agents/repository.js, and the fix is to reach agents through the container.agentsRepo facade.
review.md reports no finding of severity MEDIUM or higher against server/src/modules/notifications/repository.ts (the clean file); low-severity style notes are tolerated.
Every reported issue includes a severity, and the DB-in-service and concrete-adapter findings are ranked at least as severe as the deep-import finding.

evals.name: route-edge
evals.prompt: Here's a draft GitHub webhook receiver for DevDigest (server/src/modules/webhooks/): routes.ts and repository.ts. Review the architecture of the route before I register it in modules/index.ts — I care about whether the responsibilities are in the right layer. Write your findings to review.md — for each issue give the file, the line(s), why it's a problem in this codebase's architecture, and the concrete fix you'd make. Include a severity for each finding.
evals.expected_output: review.md listing exactly the 3 planted violations in routes.ts (unvalidated body cast with ad-hoc re-checks, business logic in the handler, direct Drizzle access in the route) with project-specific fixes, and no MEDIUM+ findings against the clean repository.ts.
expectations: review.md flags the `req.body as {...}` type-cast plus the ad-hoc typeof checks, and the fix parses the payload once at the edge with a Zod schema (route schema via fastify-type-provider-zod and/or a shared contract) instead of casting.
review.md notes that once the payload is parsed at the edge, the scattered manual re-checks are redundant (parse once at the boundary, trust the type inward).

review.md flags the pull-request status mapping / orchestration logic in the handler as business logic in the route, and the fix moves it into a service method so the handler is thin: parse, one service call, return.
review.md flags the direct Drizzle usage in the route (db.select on t.repos and db.update on t.pullRequests), and the fix moves those queries into repository methods.
review.md reports no finding of severity MEDIUM or higher against server/src/modules/webhooks/repository.ts (the clean file); low-severity style notes are tolerated.

evals.name: core-purity
evals.prompt: I added a weekly digest generator to reviewer-core (reviewer-core/src/digest/run-digest.ts) that summarizes recent review runs with an LLM. Review it for architectural fit before I export it from the package index. Write your findings to review.md — for each issue give the file, the line(s), why it's a problem in this codebase's architecture, and the concrete fix you'd make. Include a severity for each finding.
evals.expected_output: review.md listing exactly the 3 planted violations (filesystem read in the core, direct OpenRouter fetch with an env API key bypassing the injected LLMProvider, back-edge import from server) with fixes that keep reviewer-core pure, and no findings against the pure helper or the @devdigest/shared import.
expectations: review.md flags the node:fs/node:os usage (reading ~/.devdigest/run-history.json) inside reviewer-core, and the fix makes the run history an INPUT to the function (the caller — e.g. the server — does the I/O).

review.md flags the direct fetch to openrouter.ai plus the process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY read, and the fix is to use the injected LLMProvider interface instead of calling the vendor API directly from core logic.

review.md flags the import of ExternalServiceError from ../../../server/src/platform/errors.js as a forbidden core-to-server back-edge (import direction must be server -> reviewer-core -> shared), and the fix uses a core-local or shared error instead.
review.md does NOT flag the `@devdigest/shared` import (allowed inward direction) and does NOT claim the pure helper formatDigestInput must move out of reviewer-core.
review.md explains the purity invariant in substance: reviewer-core's only side effect is the injected LLMProvider, data comes in as inputs.
